key_highlights: ASX slumped as bond yields spiked and unemployment hit a 5-year high, pressuring banks and miners
RBA signals it will continue hiking despite deteriorating labour market, creating an 'interest rate pincer' for households
AUD 'trapdoor opens' amid global risk-off and US political instability (Trump/China tensions)
Housing market over halfway to largest 40-year price decline; >50% of renters financially stressed
Intergenerational Report 2026 flags urgent tax reform need, signalling future fiscal tightening
Gold and copper exploration activity robust across WA, Victoria, and international projects
Jetstar industrial action escalates; Qantas outback pricing under scrutiny
Data centre energy demand vs. grid capacity tension intensifying

sectors.trend: Negative. Bond yield spike and unemployment surge pressure NIM expectations; RBA hawkish bias supports net interest income but credit risk rising with housing decline and renter stress
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin compression risk if RBA pauses; credit losses may rise as housing falls deepen. Defensive dividend yield remains attractive but capital preservation is key

sectors.trend: Mixed. Gold exploration positive (Auric, Aureka, Forrestania, Manhattan); copper activity strong (Rio2, Sarytogan); rare earths progressing (Lindian). However, global risk-off and AUD weakness create headwinds for iron ore/coal
sectors.implications: Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NGX.AX) and explorers benefit from safe-haven flows. BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX pressured by global growth fears. Copper and rare earths names offer thematic upside

sectors.trend: Negative near-term. Data centre boom strains grid capacity; fuel cost politics (Angus Taylor vs PM) create policy uncertainty; 'energy hysteria' narrative risks overreaction
sectors.implications: SAP.AX, WDS.AX, AWE.AX face demand-side uncertainty. LNG names (WDS.AX) supported by global energy security theme. Watch for policy-driven capex shifts

sectors.trend: Negative. Jetstar industrial action, Qantas pricing backlash, Ozempic impact on food demand, renter financial stress all weigh on discretionary spend
sectors.implications: QAN.AX, JPA.AX face operational and reputational risk. WES.AX, WTW.AX pressured by consumer squeeze. CSL.AX (healthcare) relatively insulated

sectors.trend: Negative. Housing prices over halfway to 40-year decline; CBD commercial listings (lending library tower $40m); Dusty Martin portfolio haircut signal sector stress
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICOL.AX, DGL.AX) face falling valuations and rising vacancy risk. Residential REITs most exposed. Selective value in industrial/infrastructure REITs

sectors.trend: Neutral-positive. Australian small business AI adoption accelerating; global AI chip/optics trade active (Lumentum, AMD, Nvidia). Data centre energy constraints a structural risk
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (W1.AX, XRO.AX) benefit from AI adoption narrative. Energy constraints may cap data centre expansion. Global AI trade remains volatile

AUD weakness amplifies import costs and pressures domestic equities
Housing correction deepens; renter stress becomes systemic risk
Intergenerational Report 2026 signals coming tax reform and fiscal tightening
Gold/copper exploration remains a structural ASX theme amid global uncertainty
Energy infrastructure strain from data centres vs. affordability politics
Global geopolitical risk (US-China, UN tensions) elevates safe-haven demand
Industrial action in aviation sector disrupts consumer transport

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike despite 5-year high unemployment
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce leverage; favour fixed-rate debt; hold quality dividend payers with rate resilience
Hedge AUD exposure; favour export-oriented miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX) and gold as natural hedge

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Housing market 40-year decline and renter stress
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight residential REITs; monitor bank credit loss provisions; favour industrial/infrastructure REITs

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Bond yield spike / 'bonds crash stocks' scenario
risk_assessment.mitigation: Shorten duration in fixed income; favour quality equities with pricing power; avoid high-beta growth
Review tax-efficient structures; anticipate capital gains or dividend tax changes; favour franked dividend payers

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Energy infrastructure strain and policy uncertainty
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor AEMO capacity warnings; favour diversified energy producers over single-commodity exposure
Maintain 10-15% gold allocation; diversify geographically; avoid single-country concentration

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold miners and explorers as safe-haven and AUD hedge
opportunities.rationale: Robust exploration pipeline (Auric, Aureka, Forrestania, Manhattan) plus global risk-off and AUD weakness support gold prices

opportunities.recommendation: Selective copper and rare earths exposure
opportunities.rationale: Rio2 Peruvian drill, Sarytogan 452m copper, Lindian rare earths production nearing – structural supply-demand gap in transition metals
RBA hawkish bias supports NIM; 6-7% yields offer income in volatile market; credit risk manageable short-term

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce residential REIT and property exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: 40-year housing decline underway; renter stress >50%; CBD commercial listings signal structural oversupply
AUD 'trapdoor' open; RBA hiking into recession risk; interest rate pincer squeezing household balance sheets
Jetstar industrial action, Qantas pricing backlash, Ozempic demand shift, and renter stress compress consumer spending

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. ASX likely to remain under pressure from bond yield spikes, RBA hawkishness, AUD weakness, and housing decline. Banks and miners lead declines. Expect volatility around RBA communications and US-China headlines. 10-yr bond yield trajectory is the key swing factor.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. Gold/copper exploration pipeline, energy transition demand, and AI adoption provide structural themes. Intergenerational Report tax reform may create fiscal headwinds but also signal policy response. Housing correction, while painful, may stabilise within 12-18 months. Quality dividend equities remain attractive on a 6-12 month horizon.
